name: Silicon Brains: The Chips That Changed Everything
description: From the Intel 4004 and the 6502 to ARM, the Pentium, GPUs and the Apple M1: the small slices of silicon behind every computer, console and phone.

checkpoints.name: The first microprocessors
checkpoints.note: The Intel 4004 was the first microprocessor sold on the market, and the Intel 8080 powered the Altair 8800. The MOS 6502 and the Zilog Z80 were cheap enough for the Apple II and many home computers.

checkpoints.name: Chips in every PC
checkpoints.note: The x86 line began in 1978, and the IBM PC made it the standard. The Motorola 68000 powered the Macintosh and other machines with a graphical screen, and the IBM PC and Mac set the pattern for personal computers.

checkpoints.name: 32 bits and ARM
checkpoints.note: The Intel 80386 brought 32-bit computing to PCs. In Britain, Acorn, maker of the BBC Micro, designed ARM, a lean low-power chip. PowerPC, from Apple, IBM and Motorola, was a rival to x86.

checkpoints.name: Pentium and graphics
checkpoints.note: The Pentium made Intel a household brand, and the Apple Newton used ARM. 3dfx Voodoo cards brought fast 3D graphics to PC games, Nvidia GeForce was marketed as the first GPU in 1999, and Transmeta's Crusoe aimed to save power.

checkpoints.name: Phones, boards and Apple silicon
checkpoints.note: Itanium was Intel's bold 64-bit attempt that never won the market. ARM chips went into the iPhone and the Raspberry Pi, and in 2020 Apple's M1, an ARM-based design, moved the Mac away from Intel.
